articles.excerpt: When a pilot uncovers a serious performance regression, the immediate pressure to delay the entire release can lead to unnecessary project stalls. Conversely, ignoring the issue risks deploying faulty…
articles.body: When a pilot uncovers a serious performance regression, the immediate pressure to delay the entire release can lead to unnecessary project stalls. Conversely, ignoring the issue risks deploying faulty code to a wider audience. The goal is to isolate the failure to a specific component or cohort rather than treating the entire release as a failure. Quick solution: kubectl patch deployment pilot-service -p '{"spec":{"replicas":2}}' # Monitor specific metrics for the canary cohort against the baseline ./check-performance-metrics.sh --cohort canary-group --baseline production-stable Identifying the Regression Before changing your release plan, you must reproduce the regression in a controlled environment.

articles.body: title: "Why App Size Is a Product Metric (and How to Reduce It)" description: "A smaller shipped app reduces download friction, storage pressure and update pain. Here is how to approach React Native app size without making releases fragile." published: false tags: reactnative, android, appsize, performance, mobile Why App Size Is a Product Metric (and How to Reduce It) App size is easy to ignore because it is not a screen. Nobody opens an app and says, "this is a beautifully optimized artifact." But people do abandon downloads, delay updates and uninstall apps when storage gets tight. That makes app size a product experience, not just a technical metric. On a flagship phone with fast internet, a large app may be barely noticeable.

articles.title: The Undo Button Test: How Software Taught Me to Stop Overthinking Small Decisions
articles.excerpt: Before any big decision, I've started asking one boring question: how expensive is the undo? It sounds too simple to be useful. But it came straight out of how we build software, and it's changed how…
articles.body: Before any big decision, I've started asking one boring question: how expensive is the undo? It sounds too simple to be useful. But it came straight out of how we build software, and it's changed how I spend my worry. Two kinds of changes In software teams we quietly sort every change into two piles. The first pile is easy to revert. You change a button label, tweak a color, or put a new feature behind a switch you can turn off. If it goes wrong, you roll it back in minutes. Nobody needs a meeting for this. You ship it, watch what happens, and adjust. The second pile holds the one-way doors. Deleting customer data. A database change you can't reverse. Sending an email to every user. Once it's done, it's done.
articles.author: Serghei Pogor

articles.title: Why Exit Scripts Are Too Late: Stopping Post-Compaction Retry Spirals in Coding Agents
articles.excerpt: A few months ago, I briefly thought I had solved coding-agent governance in twenty minutes. I binned half of a bloated 3,000-word rules file and replaced it with a strict post-edit verification script…
articles.body: A few months ago, I briefly thought I had solved coding-agent governance in twenty minutes. I binned half of a bloated 3,000-word rules file and replaced it with a strict post-edit verification script. Any forbidden SQL pattern, stray dependency, or missing boundary check tripped a blocking non-zero exit ( exit 1 in POSIX wrappers; exit 2 in Claude Code hooks). No begging in system prompts - just deterministic checks. Twelve minutes later, I came back expecting a clean diff and found the agent on Turn 14 of a remarkably polite loop with the shell: failing, apologising, leaving half-patched files on disk, renaming a local variable, and walking straight back into the same error. The annoying part? The exit script was working flawlessly.

articles.title: HTML to video: 5 ways to turn a web page into an MP4, plus a worked example
articles.excerpt: You have a web page with an animation in it, and someone wants an MP4. You press a screen recorder, the animation stutters on the slow frames, and the file is only as smooth as your laptop was that mi…
articles.body: You have a web page with an animation in it, and someone wants an MP4. You press a screen recorder, the animation stutters on the slow frames, and the file is only as smooth as your laptop was that minute. This post is about getting from HTML to video without that problem. HTML to video: the short answer To turn HTML into a video, open the page in a browser and either record it while it plays or render it frame by frame. Rendering means you pause the animation, move it to each frame's exact time, take a screenshot, and encode the screenshots into an MP4 with FFmpeg. Recording is quicker to set up. Rendering frame by frame gives a smooth file on any machine, because how fast the computer draws no longer matters.

articles.title: What Is the Difference Between an AI Model and an AI Agent?
articles.excerpt: An AI model takes text in and sends text back. An AI agent is the program around a model that lets it act. The agent gives the model a goal and tools, like a calendar or a booking system, runs the too…
articles.body: An AI model takes text in and sends text back. An AI agent is the program around a model that lets it act. The agent gives the model a goal and tools, like a calendar or a booking system, runs the tools the model asks for, and keeps going until the job is done or it hits a limit. I'm strict about the AI model vs AI agent line, because the labels have gotten loose. This month's model launches came with agent claims attached. SD Times reported that Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2, released November 9, can orchestrate agent teams. It's still a model. On its own, it doesn't book anything. The best counter-argument is that the line has blurred, since models now choose tools by themselves. They do choose.

articles.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to December's full Cold Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..
